reviewStandard: Scientific identity, morphology, controlled identifiers, caption limits, non-diagnostic framing, provenance, accessibility, and publication files passed the WikiBiome scientific media policy before promotion. The original prompt remains immutable provenance; a separate human output audit reconciles what is actually visible with all published metadata.

assets.scientificFinding: The original A. colihominis description reports anaerobic rods, while an emended description based on electron microscopy reports nonmotile pleomorphic thin bacilli with occasional oval terminal spores, including re-observation of spores in the original strains.
assets.visualReview: Seven thin bacilli span restrained straight-to-curved pleomorphism with one loose pair; exactly one cell contains an oval terminal spore and no cell bears an appendage. No host, stool, blood, label, or diagnostic narrative is shown.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Seven cellular bodies, including one loose pair; one cell contains one oval terminal spore.

assets.proposedAlt: Seven thin Anaerotruncus bacilli, including a loose pair and one cell with an oval terminal endospore, on a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Anaerotruncus morphology. A. colihominis is a nonmotile pleomorphic bacillus whose emended description reports occasional oval terminal spores; this reconstruction is not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of pleomorphic Anaerotruncus rods and the occasional terminal endospore documented for A. colihominis.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies Aspergillus as fungal genus NCBITaxon:5052. CDC public-health microscopy documents smooth hyaline conidiophores ending in a bulbous vesicle with biseriate metulae, phialides, and chains of spherical conidia, while CDC case work emphasizes species-level variation in these structures.
assets.visualReview: One septate hyphal segment supports a smooth conidiophore and one organized radiating head whose vesicle, biseriate supporting cells, and short spherical conidial chains remain legible; no moldy room, host, culture plate, or generic spore cloud is present.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: One septate hyphal segment, one conidiophore, and one organized radiating conidial head with its component structures legible.

assets.proposedAlt: An Aspergillus conidial head with a smooth stalk, bulbous vesicle, two supporting cell layers, and radiating short chains of spherical conidia.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative biseriate Aspergillus conidial-head morphology. Vesicle shape, phialide arrangement, and conidial form vary across species; this reconstruction is genus-level and not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of a septate Aspergillus hypha, smooth conidiophore, vesicle, metulae, phialides, and conidial chains.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI retains Atopobium as genus NCBITaxon:1380 and A. minutum as its current type species NCBITaxon:1381. The original genus proposal and DSMZ type-strain record support a Gram-positive elliptical-to-rod treatment, while species transferred to Lancefieldella or Fannyhessea are excluded from the visual scope.
assets.visualReview: Nine small elliptical-to-short-rod cells occur as four singles, one pair, and one three-cell chain without appendages, spores, host scene, labels, or biofilm. The image does not encode the obsolete A. parvulum or A. vaginae combinations.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Nine cellular bodies: four singles, one pair, and one three-cell chain.

assets.proposedAlt: Nine small Atopobium cells ranging from elliptical forms to short rods, arranged singly, as a pair, and in a three-cell chain on a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative morphology for the current Atopobium genus, centered on A. minutum-like elliptical to short rods. Species now assigned to Lancefieldella or Fannyhessea are outside this image's scope; it is not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of current-genus Atopobium cells occurring singly, in a pair, and in a short chain.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI recognizes Lancefieldella parvula as the current name for NCBITaxon:1382 and lists Atopobium parvulum only as a homotypic synonym. The canonical route therefore uses a superseded combination.
assets.visualReview: No image was generated because publication under the obsolete route title would misstate the current scientific identity.
assets.requiredResolution: Rename or redirect the canonical route to Lancefieldella parvula, or explicitly scope the article as a historical synonym page keyed to NCBITaxon:1382, before media review proceeds.

assets.requiredResolution: Rename or redirect the canonical route to Fannyhessea vaginae, or explicitly scope the article as a historical synonym page keyed to NCBITaxon:82135, before media review proceeds.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI identifies the emended Bacillus genus as NCBITaxon:1386, now limited principally to the subtilis and cereus clades. Taxonomic and electron-microscopy sources support aerobic vegetative rods and dormant endospores, with species-level variation in spore position and cell morphology.
assets.visualReview: Five robust rods include one pair, one central and one subterminal non-swelling internal spore, plus one separate mature oval spore; no flagella, capsule, anthrax-specific chain, host material, labels, or disease symbolism are shown.

outputAudit.observedSubjectDescription: Five rod-shaped cellular bodies, two internal endospores, and one separate mature oval spore.

assets.proposedAlt: Five Bacillus rods, two containing oval endospores, beside one separate mature spore on a pale cool field.
assets.proposedCaption: Representative Bacillus sensu stricto vegetative rods and dormant endospores. Spore position, cell shape, and motility vary by species; this reconstruction is genus-level and not diagnostic.
assets.proposedDescription: WikiBiome microscopy-informed reconstruction of representative Bacillus rods, internal endospores, and one free mature spore.
